We reviewed the July 2026 billing record showing 910 kWh and the billed amount, the energy and fixed charge rate components used to calculate that amount, the two actual period-end register reads (30,500 kWh on 2026-06-30 and 31,150 kWh on 2026-07-31), the monthly usage history for April–July 2026, and the meter event log entry noting a communication loss on 2026-07-14. We also checked the supplied adjustments and prior-contact records and found none.

What we found
Confirmed: the July bill is for 910 kWh and the amount billed equals 910 kWh at USD 0.22/kWh plus the USD 12 fixed charge. Confirmed: the meter register reads on 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-31 are recorded as actual and produce a register delta of 650 kWh. The bill amount matches the posted rates applied to 910 kWh, which is why your total for July appears higher than June. However, the two actual meter register reads supplied indicate only 650 kWh of register change for the July window, so the origin of the additional 260 kWh in the bill is not shown in the records we have.
